title: The Promise Was Divinely Free
description: The Promise Was Divinely Free in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 134, headed “Circumcision abolished”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The pro-mise was di-vine-ly free, Ex-ten-sive was the grace; "I will the God of A-brah'm be, "And of his nu-merous race."

lines: "I will the God of Abrah'm be,
He said; and with a bloody seal
Long did the Sons of Abrah'm feel
Till God's own Son, descending low,
Gave his own flesh to bleed;
And Gentiles taste the blessing now,
The God of Abrah'm claims our praise,
And Christ the Lord in gentler ways

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
